 Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Georges Niang, Yaxel Lendeborg and Draymond Green will start Wednesday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 Gui Santos (knee) is out, opening a spot in the Warriors’ starting lineup. Niang fills the void, and he’s averaged 6.0 points per game in his first four appearances this season. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Yaxel Lendeborg 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #1

 Yaxel Lendeborg (foot) participated in shootaround ahead of Wednesday’s game against the Timberwolves. 
 Lendeborg is still listed as questionable, but this is a good sign. The rookie has been fantastic early on and should continue to put up gaudy stats, assuming he’s available for this game. If something changes, Golden State could turn to Georges Niang in the starting unit. 
 Yaxel Lendeborg 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Yaxel Lendeborg (foot) is questionable for Wednesday’s matchup with the Timberwolves. 
 Lendeborg has been Golden State’s best player through the first week of the season, and his 31/12/6 line on Monday led to an upset road win over the Nuggets. If Lendeborg is forced to sit out against Minnesota, Will Richard and Georges Niang could see more run, but neither carry much streaming appeal for fantasy hoops. 
 Georges Niang 
 GSW 
 Forward 
 #20 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Warriors signed Georges Niang to a one-year deal worth $3.9 million. 
 Thanks to a foot injury suffered before the start of training camp, Niang did not play at all in 2025-26 after agreeing to a one-year deal with the Jazz. The veteran forward, who was sent to Memphis as part of the Jaren Jackson Jr. trade, was waived shortly thereafter. Playing for the Cavaliers and Hawks, Niang averaged 9.9 points, 3.4 rebounds, 1.4 assists and 2.1 three-pointers per game in 2024-25, shooting 40.6 percent from beyond the arc. He’ll provide the Warriors with added frontcourt depth but is unlikely to be in a position where he consistently affects fantasy basketball. 
 Georges Niang 
 FA 
 Forward 
 #20 
 NBA insider Marc Stein reports that the Warriors have expressed some interest in free agents Georges Niang and Brandon Williams. 
 The Warriors have roster spots to fill, but not much cap space to do it. Due to a left foot injury, Niang did not play at all in 2025-26, beginning his year with the Jazz before being sent to Memphis as part of the Jaren Jackson Jr. trade. As for Williams, he appeared in 66 games for the Mavericks last season, averaging 13.0 points, 2.9 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 0.9 steals in 22.2 minutes. While he did record career-best averages, Williams’ increased opportunities came as a result of Kyrie Irving missing the entire season with a torn ACL. He and Niang are capable contributors if they were to land with the Warriors, but neither qualifies as a must-draft player in most leagues. 
 Georges Niang 
 FA 
 Forward 
 #20 
 Grizzlies intend to waive Georges Niang. 
 Niang was sent from Utah to Memphis as part of the Jaren Jackson Jr. trade, but the Grizzlies won’t keep him around. The veteran forward will look to find a new team to join for the second half of the season, where he will likely end up as just a depth piece. 
 Georges Niang 
 MEM 
 Forward 
 #31 
 Georges Niang, Walter Clayton Jr., Taylor Hendricks, Kyle Anderson and three future first-round picks have been traded to the Grizzlies in exchange for Jaren Jackson Jr., John Konchar, Jock Landale and Vince Williams Jr. 
 Niang, whom the Jazz signed to a one-year deal during the offseason, has yet to appear in a game this season due to a stress reaction in his left foot. His addition to the Grizzlies roster won’t affect fantasy basketball, as he does not have a timeline to return to action. 
 Georges Niang 
 UTA 
 Forward 
 #31 
 Georges Niang (foot) will be re-evaluated in two weeks. 
 Sidelined by a stress reaction in the fourth metatarsal of his left foot, Niang has yet to appear in a game this season. According to the Jazz, it will be at least two more weeks before he has the opportunity to play. Niang’s continued absence does not directly affect fantasy basketball, but it does leave more minutes available for some of Utah’s younger frontcourt players. 
 Georges Niang 
 UTA 
 Forward 
 #31 
 Georges Niang (foot) will be re-evaluated in 10 to 14 days. 
 Niang, who has yet to play a game this season, is dealing with a stress reaction in his left fourth metatarsal. Given the lack of activity, even if he’s given a clean bill of health at the next evaluation, there will likely be a ramp-up period to bring Niang’s conditioning up to par. There’s no need to stash him in an IL slot. 
 Georges Niang 
 UTA 
 Forward 
 #31 
 Georges Niang (foot) is progressing through rehab and will be re-evaluated in 2-3 weeks. 
 Niang was given a two-week timeline for re-evaluation on September 27, but he’s still not ready to return. The new evaluation on October 12 means he’ll be sidelined through the start of the regular season. Once he’s back on the court, there’s no guarantee Niang will play enough minutes to be a viable fantasy option in 12-team leagues. 
 Georges Niang 
 UTA 
 Forward 
 #31 
 The Jazz announced Saturday that Georges Niang (foot) will be re-evaluated in two weeks. 
 Per a team release, Niang suffered a stress reaction in the fourth metatarsal in his left foot during offseason training. As a result, he’ll be sidelined for two weeks before the team’s medical staff re-evaluates the veteran forward’s foot. Niang was traded twice this offseason, first being sent from Atlanta to Boston before the Celtics moved him to Utah. Once healthy, he’ll play rotation minutes, but the question is how much due to Utah being in the midst of a rebuild.

 Desmond Bane put up 13 points (3-of-14 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, a steal, two blocks, and two 3-pointers in 99-129 loss to Raptors. 
 It was a bad night for Bane as he couldn’t get shots to fall against the Raptors. Bane in the past two seasons has shot 48.4% from the field, but he hasn’t shot very well this season. There is a good track record to indicate that there will be a bounce back from Bane and to not panic too much about his efficiency. He at least got you five rebounds and four assists to give you some value.

 Tristan Da Silva with 20 points (8-of-10 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, and four 3-pointers in 30 minutes off the bench against Raptors. 
 Anthony Black didn’t have it tonight, so Da Silva got some more extended run and did not disappoint. He’s not someone that is inherently a scorer, but he was hitting shots tonight when not many other people on the Magic were scoring against the Raptors. He’s a points and 3-point streamer if you’re looking for it in but he won’t shoot as efficiently as he did most nights.

 Franz Wagner had 15 points (4-of-11 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, and seven turnovers in blowout loss to Raptors.
 Franz was one of the only players that could get shots up in this game. The Magic struggled with efficiency as they dealt with the Raptors aggressive defense, but you can see it affected Franz with the 7 turnovers. The Magic will play the Raptors again on Friday and will get a second chance at redemption where he will look to have a better performance.

 Pelle Larsson had 17 points (6-of-12 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists, one steal and two three-pointers against the Hawks on Wednesday. 
 Larsson has recorded at least 12 points, at least four assists, at least one steal and at least one three-pointer in three consecutive games. He’s also played at least 31 minutes in three consecutive games and had at least six rebounds in two of the last three games. Larsson is turning out to be a key bench player for Heat and worth considering picking up given his recent production.

 Kelly Oubre with 15 points (5-of-10 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, and a three taking over Haliburton in the starting lineup. 
 With no Haliburton and Zubac tonight, Oubre’s scoring was much needed in the Pacers come back. From a fantasy perspective, he doesn’t provide much outside of decent scoring and occasional rebounding, so he’s fine if you need a boost in those categories, but he will have other games where the shot isn’t there and there’s not a lot there from a fantasy perspective.

 Pascal Siakam had a monster 26 points (11-of-17 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, three assists, and a steal on Wednesday. 
Pascal did his best to lead the Pacers without Haliburton in this game and did a good job scoring the ball. He was a monster on the boards as the Pacers out hustled the 76ers in this game. We have at least two weeks before Haliburton comes back, so sit back and enjoy the production but also recognize that it might come down a bit once Haliburton comes back.

 Bam Adebayo had 24 points (8-of-16 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and three steals against the Hawks on Wednesday. 
 Adebayo bounced back nicely after scoring only eight points in Monday’s loss to the Mavericks. The 24 points Adebayo had are his season-high through five games. He’ll look to keep up his scoring against the Pacers on Friday.

 Andrew Nembhard had 18 points (5-of-16 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, fourteen assists, and a three in loss on Wednesday to the Sixers. 
 Nembhard got plenty of shot attempts, assists and to the line. You can see the framework of his fantasy game when Haliburton is out. He was passing the ball, and he was the reason why the Pacers got back in this game in the third quarter. Nembhard won’t shoot 31% from the field very often, so this performance can be even better if he hit a few more shots.

 Anfernee Simons 
 PHI 
 Guard 
 #5

 Anfernee Simons scored 20 points (7-of-11 FGs), got three rebounds, an assist, a steal, and six 3-pointers in win over the Pacers. 
 Simons will have games where he hits 3’s and provides the 76ers bench with some much-needed scoring. Simons has been in a slump but it’s good to see him have a bounce back game. He’s currently shooting 35.7% from the field and a regression to the mean would indicate that he’s going to have a few more performances to balance out the bad shooting from this past week. In deeper leagues, he’s a nice streamer for points and 3-pointers.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo had 24 points (11-of-18 FGs, 2-of-5 FTs), 18 rebounds, three assists, one block and one steal in Wednesday’s 129-117 victory over the Hawks. 
 Antetokounmpo’s fantasy production hadn’t suffered despite the slow start by his new team the Heat. After an 0-4 start to the season, Miami finally picked up its first win against the Hawks Wednesday. Antetokounmpo was excellent again as he grabbed a game-high 18 rebounds, which was at least twice as many as anyone else.
